questions.text: Should the board answer ARP requests for 192.168.1.50?
questions.default: Yes, answer ARP requests for LOCAL_IP with LOCAL_MAC.
questions.reason: Other machines cannot send echo requests to the board on the same LAN without an ARP reply, so ping fails otherwise.
questions.answer: Yes, answer ARP requests for LOCAL_IP with LOCAL_MAC.

questions.text: What MAC address should the board use?
questions.default: 02:50:49:4E:47:01, locally administered and unicast, bytes spelling PI in the middle.
questions.reason: The request says give the board a MAC address but gives no value; a locally administered address avoids clashing with a vendor OUI.
questions.answer: 02:50:49:4E:47:01, locally administered and unicast, bytes spelling PI in the middle.

questions.text: Is the PHY wired for RMII with a 50 MHz reference clock from the FPGA, or for RGMII?
questions.default: RMII with a 50 MHz reference clock generated in the FPGA.
questions.reason: RMII needs fewer pins and a single 50 MHz clock; the choice must match the board schematic and the XDC pin constraints.
questions.answer: RMII with a 50 MHz reference clock generated in the FPGA.

questions.text: Is any MDIO configuration of the PHY needed (for example to force 100 Mbps or disable auto-negotiation)?
questions.default: No, use strap defaults with auto-negotiation.
questions.reason: The request does not state a link speed; MDIO adds a state machine that is only needed if link negotiation fails.
questions.answer: No, use strap defaults with auto-negotiation.

questions.text: How long should the LED stay lit after each reply?
questions.default: LED_PULSE_CYCLES = 10000000 clock cycles, which is 100 ms at 100 MHz, long enough for a person to see.
questions.reason: The request says light an LED each time a reply is sent but gives no duration; a single reply would otherwise be too short to see.
questions.answer: LED_PULSE_CYCLES = 10000000 clock cycles, which is 100 ms at 100 MHz, long enough for a person to see.

questions.default: LED0, the first user LED of the board.
questions.reason: The request says an LED without naming one; LED0 is the first user LED and is easy to find.
questions.answer: LED0, the first user LED of the board.

questions.text: What should happen to echo requests sent to the broadcast address or to a multicast IPv4 address?
questions.default: Ignore them and send no reply.
questions.reason: The request asks for replies to requests sent to the board; replying to broadcast would reply to every machine on the subnet.
questions.answer: Ignore them and send no reply.

questions.text: What is the largest frame accepted?
questions.default: 1518 bytes including FCS; larger frames are discarded.
questions.reason: The request gives no size limit; the standard Ethernet maximum keeps the frame buffer to one BRAM.
questions.answer: 1518 bytes including FCS; larger frames are discarded.

questions.text: Should the design check the FCS of received frames?
questions.default: Yes, discard received frames with a bad FCS.
questions.reason: A corrupted request would otherwise be answered with a corrupted reply.
questions.answer: Yes, discard received frames with a bad FCS.

questions.text: Should fragmented IPv4 echo requests be answered?
questions.reason: Reassembly needs a buffer and state that the request does not ask for; ping from normal machines is not fragmented.

questions.text: What does the design do with the CPU reset button when the PHY is still in reset?
questions.default: Hold eth_rst_n low while cpu_resetn is low and release it 1000 clk cycles after cpu_resetn goes high.
questions.reason: The request says reset with the CPU reset button; the PHY needs its reset release sequence before link.
questions.answer: Hold eth_rst_n low while cpu_resetn is low and release it 1000 clk cycles after cpu_resetn goes high.
